title: Christian V to the envoys Jens Juel and Christoffer Lindenov in Stockholm, Copenhagen, 25 May 1673, closing cipher block (catalogue 2528 = lead 2531, Rigsarkivet TKUA Sverige): syllabic code rebuilt from the 1674 interlinear decipherments and tested on a held-out order, read in part

documents.shelfmark: Copenhagen, Rigsarkivet, TKUA, Speciel del, Sverige, Jens Juels gesandtskabsarkiv; Arkivalieronline unit 261588, images 7-11 (closing cipher block: image 10 foot and image 11)
documents.route: Christian V of Denmark (countersigned Griffenfeld) -> Jens Juel and Christoffer Lindenov, envoys in Stockholm

plaintext.source: loose chancery leaf (image 9 right): decipherment of the first cipher block only; its filmed side ends with that block, its verso was not filmed. The closing block has no decipherment.

transcription.source: Arkivalieronline images of unit 261588 (api.rigsarkivet.dk, full size); images not reproduced
transcription.notes: Closing block transcribed by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent (11 Nov 2026) before any key was applied to it, and frozen; sign shapes later sorted on a sign sheet (TABLE-SIGNES.tsv): our label Q covers q barred (i) and a hooked 4 (r). No blind re-reading yet.

system.summary: Danish royal chancery code of 1673-74: three-digit groups in alphabetical blocks (five syllables per initial, e.g. 417-421 ba be bi bo bu, 482-486 da ... du, then words of that initial: 585 haffuer, 595 hvor); names and countries in 2xx-3xx (284 Sverig, 309 Holland, 321 Franckrig); small numbers and signs for single letters (4 t, 5 e, 18 r, ff n, S t, Z n); many Danish words left in clear.
system.notes: Some signs change value between the hand of 1673 and the hands of 1674 (barred m = k in 1673, u in 1674; 3 = u in 1673; 29 = x in 1673, i in 1674). Groups of the closing block with no value anywhere in the volume: 32, 320, 348, 384, 646, 906.

prior_solution.where: The first cipher block of the same order is deciphered on a loose chancery leaf (image 9 right); three sibling orders of 1674 in the same code (images 32-43) are deciphered between the lines. The closing block has no decipherment. Catalogue 2528 vetting (Daniel Bourdeau, 11 Nov 2026): DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry nothing; Danmark-Norges Traktater 6 does not print the order; lead 2531: Vaupell, Jørgensen, Fryxell, Danske Samlinger nothing.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (every decipherment goes to Daniel; a partial reading may be published if explained; protocol hashed before each single measurement). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed the cipher and the 1674 glosses, made the sign table, rebuilt the key, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, sign table, key, protocols, measurement, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Both cipher blocks of 25 May 1673 transcribed (closing block 197 tokens, frozen before any key was applied); the loose leaf of image 9 read; four sub-agents transcribed the cipher groups and interlinear glosses of the three orders of 1674 (images 32-43, about 3,640 groups).

Key rebuilt from the 1674 glosses (weighted majority per group) and the 1673 leaf; sign labels of the different transcribers mapped to canonical signs on a sign sheet; alphabetical syllable blocks of five recognised (14 initials).

Protocol 1 (hashed beforehand): key v1 applied once to the 1673 closing block, scored by Danish lexical cover. Declared bar: COV >= 0.70, and at least 0.06 above the best of 200 permuted keys and of 200 group shuffles. Result: COV 0.722, best permuted key 0.668 (margin 0.054, bar 0.06: failed by 0.006), best shuffle 0.648. The test failed; the block was not measured again.

Protocol 2 (hashed beforehand; a different test, on other material): key v2 rebuilt from orders A and B only, decoded once against the glosses of the held-out order C (6 Oct 1674, images 42-43): 0.849 of 776 gloss segments exact vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.144 and best of 20 shifts 0.035; bar >= 0.65 and +0.40 over each control, met. It covers the three-digit code groups; the 1673 values of signs and small numbers rest on the loose leaf. What had been seen of C is declared in validation.txt.

Closing block read by sense with key v2 (+ 486 du, 534 fu, 590 huis added after the measurement): 68 cipher words, 48 certain, 10 probable, 3 restored, 6 unresolved (the contributor's count of certain + probable: 86.8%).

Integration check of pull request #409 after an independent verification. Both measurement scripts re-run in a scratch copy: test 2 gives 0.849 (659/776), 0.144, 0.035 again and KEY-v2 rebuilds byte-identical; test 1 re-run with the repository's lang/lexicons/da.json.gz (same SHA-256 as the missing working/da.json.gz) gives 0.722 / 0.668 / 0.648 again, a failure. 196 of 197 tokens agree with images 10-11; T04 841? looked at again at full size: overwritten, 541 at least as likely, left open. Corrections: read share set to 48/68 = 0.706 (certain words only, README read bar); outcome.key partial with codes_open; 29 = x (1673 hand, from the leaf's 'extenderes') added to key.tsv, decryption.txt made to agree with reading.md, Exempel moved from restored to probable.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the decipherments of the time written between the lines of two sibling orders of 1674 in the same unit and from the chancery leaf deciphering the first block of 1673; its three-digit groups were tested on a third glossed order held out, then it was applied to the closing block of 1673, which has no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decryption.txt: cipher tokens with a value in key.tsv, 190 of 197 (the seven tokens of groups 32, 320, 348, 384 twice, 646, 906 have none). Share of words read as sense is lower, see fraction_coherent.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests against ground truth (not docs/_validate.py), both re-run at integration with the same figures. The verdict is that of test 2 (PROTOCOLE-2, SHA-256 9db1cf5e..., hashed with KEY-v2 5334c7aa... and the scorer before the single run): held-out order of 6 Oct 1674 (images 42-43), exact 0.849 (659/776 gloss segments), best of 200 permuted keys 0.144, best of 20 shifts 0.035; bar >= 0.65 and +0.40 over each control, met. It covers the three-digit code groups (94 of the 197 tokens of the 1673 block); the 1673 values of signs and small numbers rest on the loose leaf. Not blind in the strict sense: the held-out pairs had been seen in aggregate and image 43 at reduced size (declared). Test 1 (PROTOCOLE.md), Danish lexical cover on the 1673 block itself, FAILED: 0.722 against 0.668 for the best permuted key, margin 0.054 where 0.06 was required. Order of events by the contributor's record (single commit, his own timestamps).

credits.note: the Danish chancery decipherments of the time: interlinear glosses of the orders of 21 July, 3 Oct and 6 Oct 1674 (images 32-43) and the loose leaf deciphering the first block of 25 May 1673 (image 9 right); the key was rebuilt from them and validated on the third order

transcription of the 1673 order and of the 1674 glosses; key rebuilt from the 1674 interlinear decipherments and the 1673 leaf, tested on the held-out order of 6 Oct 1674 (0.849 vs 0.144); closing block of 25 May 1673 read in part and translated; with AI agents

gaps.detail: seen at the resolution served online; not yet re-read blind

texts.label: Christian V to Juel and Lindenov, Copenhagen 25 May 1673, closing cipher block
texts.summary: On the salute at sea in the Sound: if the Swedes ask that their warships pass the Danish castles without striking, the envoys are to answer that any exemption is only a temporary indulgence, on the footing already laid down that other crowned heads and Sweden itself, whose example they allege, claim no such salute; and that the king will never give up a right his ancestors held unchallenged for so many years.

reading_review.by: integration check (AI agent, for the project), after the contributor's agent
reading_review.note: Read as Danish sentences against decryption.txt and translation.md: coherent on the salute in the Sound from 'uden strygen woris Slotte at passere' to the end, and the translation follows; the first line and a half (groups 384, 348, 320) does not form. 48 of 68 cipher words certain, 12 probable, 2 restored, 6 unresolved: read in part. No human has read it.

outcome.notes: New partial reading: the closing block of 25 May 1673 had no decipherment. The key is reusable (key.tsv, CC BY 4.0) for the other orders of this code. The contributor sent no image; one crop of image 11 was added to the site at integration, credited to Rigsarkivet.
